title: KS-921 residues: five Dockerfile shapes the re-link guard cannot read, an nginx final stage it can NEVER pass, and one A_FAIL branch no test can red
description:
## KS-921 gate residues F-3, F-6, F-7 — five legitimate Dockerfile shapes the guard cannot read, one it can never pass, and one branch no test can red

From the #870 gate. Deliberately **not** fixed in that PR: F-1/F-2/F-4/F-5 were, because they are false cleans and false blocks that bite today; these three are shapes with **no live exposure** and one design question that deserves a decision rather than a patch.

**Live exposure today is zero, measured:** all seven frontend Dockerfiles use nginx/alpine final stages, **none** consumes `shared-builder`, and no frontend source imports `@secuura/shared` (0 files). So nothing in the tree hits these paths now — which is exactly why they should be recorded rather than left to be discovered by whoever first writes one.

### F-6 comes first, because it is the one with no answer

**For an nginx final stage the guard offers no route forward.** A static-serving final stage legitimately has no `node_modules` at all, so clause A's `final stage writes node_modules nowhere` fires and there is no way to make the file green except by adding a pointless `node_modules` write purely to satisfy the check.

**A guard with no green path for a legitimate shape is a design question, not a bug.** The options are roughly: exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and consumes no builder tree; require an explicit opt-out marker; or narrow the class further so such files never enter it. **This is the first item on this ticket and it should be decided before anything below it is coded**, because the answer changes what the other shapes need.

### F-3 — five legitimate shapes the parser cannot read

1. **BuildKit heredoc** — `RUN <<EOF … EOF`. The parser joins on trailing `\` and treats each logical line independently, so a re-link inside a heredoc body is invisible.
2. **An nginx final stage with no** `node_modules` — see F-6.
3. **The non-final-stage write.** Clause A is stated over the FINAL stage. A Dockerfile whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM` in the file (a valid multi-target build) is judged against the wrong stage.
4. `npm i` **shorthand.** The install detector matches `npm ci|install`; `npm i` alone is not matched, so a stage installing that way reads as writing no `node_modules`.
5. **The JSON** `COPY` **form** — `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]`. Valid Dockerfile, unreadable to a whitespace-token parser.

Plus the two parser edges the gate noted.

### F-7 — and this one is the same family as three tickets already on this board

**The** `A_FAIL` **branch for "final stage writes node_modules nowhere" is pinned by NO test.**

Measured 2026-09-06, by neutering it (`note("A_FAIL", …)` → `note("A_OK", …)`) and re-running:

```
suite with the branch neutered ............ 26 passed, 0 failed
"final stage has NO" ...................... pinned by 4 cells
"runs BEFORE the last instruction" ........ pinned by 1 cell
"runs after a non-root" ................... pinned by 1 cell
"writes node_modules nowhere" ............. pinned by 0 cells
```

The tamper was restored and the file verified byte-identical by sha256.

**A branch no cell can red is a check that cannot fail** — and it is the fourth mechanism of that family on this board tonight, alongside [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926) (a check nothing runs), [KS-927](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-927) (a check running with the half that would notice already dead) and [KS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-928) (a check whose wiring is unasserted). Here the guard runs, the suite runs, the wiring is asserted — **and one branch of it still cannot be shown to work.**

Note the ordering trap for whoever fixes it: this branch is also *unreachable in practice for the current class*, since every one of the 25 files writes `node_modules` in its final stage. Pinning it needs a fixture, and the fixture is the nginx shape from F-6 — **so F-6's decision and F-7's cell are the same piece of work.**

### Fix shape

Decide F-6 first. Then a cell per F-3 shape, each red-proofed by the shape it describes, and the F-7 cell falling out of F-6's chosen semantics. **No shape should be "supported" without a cell that reds without it** — the guard already shipped one branch without that and this ticket is the receipt.

*Filed by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the #870 gate at Wednesday's direction to ticket rather than widen that PR. The F-7 measurement above is mine; the shapes are the gate's.*

nodes.body: **BLUF:** Delivered: PR 876 (F-3 node_modules write spellings, 8aefd2b06bf2), PR 886 (F-QA-2 message, 61df129e9c58), PR 879 (852e1fff773b) and PR 874 (bc067e3e9182) are merged on develop, and PR 1121 (4a61519883fe) adds the KS-957 red-proof of the tooling tokens; all are in the tree deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today) and are developer tooling and tests. Left open: residue by this ticket's own words. The 2026-09-13 held-open comment records that F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes were deliberately not fixed (the heredoc case is a stated rule at `check-shared-relink.sh:218-224`, not a fix) and that no suite cell names a runtime stage that is not the last FROM. The only commit since then on the deployed history that names KS-930 is PR 1121, which is KS-957's.

## CORRECTION to the 2026-09-14 08:00:51Z record above (comment `93033711`) — "identical on the base (not regressions)" is FALSE for two of the four spellings, by measurement at the named base (merge seat s228, on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 09:17:07Z)

The record carried Peter's finding-4 sentence from the #879 review ("not regressions; all of these behave identically on the base") for four spellings. The tier-2 round-2 gate on #879 measured each against the guard at the PR's own base `a0ad0a084` (blob `9141597bd`), at develop M38 (`7426b1874`) and at the head `0374bec00` (`d41c79538`), same fixture skeleton, both modes (report `2026-09-14-879-ks945-tier2-r2` §8 FINDING 3a; evidence `17_finding4_at_base.out`, `20_regression_fixture_full_output.txt`):

- `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` — **rc 1 at `a0ad0a084` and at M38 (BLOCKED), rc 0 at the head (CLEAN)** → a regression of #879, not a pre-existing gap.
- `RUN corepack yarn install` — **rc 1 at `a0ad0a084` and at M38, rc 0 at the head** → a regression of #879.
- `RUN npx create-vite my-app` — clean at base and head alike (as recorded).
- `RUN sh -c "npm ci"` — clean at base and head alike (as recorded).

The sentence in the record is therefore wrong about two of its four members. Source of the error: the review body asserted "identical on the base" without a base/head table (unlike its finding 2, which had one); s229 transcribed it faithfully on Wednesday's brief, which instructed the seat to route the finding as Peter wrote it — the error is Wednesday's brief's, carried into the record, and is corrected here by the gate's instrument. The two regressed spellings are members of the FINDING 1 class in the comment above (the wrapper/prefix-before-the-manager mechanism), which this ticket's class-(a) build closes. Nothing else in the record changes: the disposition ("the natural limit of a line-oriented guard, better on a ticket") stands; #879 merged onto develop by Wednesday's ruling with this class disclosed. Facts only; no state change.

## FINDING 1 from the tier-2 round-2 gate on PR #879 (KS-945), 2026-09-14 09:12:12Z — the generalised class this ticket's class-(a) build must cover: a wrapper or prefix before the manager hides an install after the re-link (merge seat s228, on Wednesday's ADDENDUM 09:17:07Z)

**The finding, as the gate wrote it (report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-14-879-ks945-tier2-r2/report.md` §8, Major):** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh:169-216` (`pm_writes`), specifically `:192` `if (a[i] != "npm" && a[i] != "yarn" && a[i] != "pnpm") continue` after the `:191` skip loop that steps over only `""`, the bare word `sudo`, and `NAME=value` — reads only the LEADING word of each separator-split segment, so ANY word in front of the manager hides an install from the guard. **Twelve spellings are BLOCKED by the guard at the PR's own base `a0ad0a084` and at develop M38, and are certified `1 of 1 clean` at the head `0374bec00`** — a false-CLEAN regression, the #851 direction: `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` · `RUN env NODE_ENV=production npm ci` · `RUN exec npm ci` · `RUN time npm ci` · `RUN nice npm ci` · `RUN nohup npm ci` · `RUN command npm ci` · `RUN echo x | xargs npm ci` · `RUN sudo -u node npm ci` · `RUN ./node_modules/.bin/npm ci` · `RUN corepack yarn install` · `RUN corepack pnpm i`. Oracle: Purpose (the guard's own header and the PR's comment — "a false clean is neither visible nor cheap… an unknown verb now blocks"), History (the base caught these), Product (the COPY clause of the same file states "widening what the parser SEES can only ADD node_modules writes, never remove one, so this direction fails safe" — the RUN clause narrowed what it sees). Repro: `git show 0374bec00:Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh > g.sh`; write `d/services/thing/Dockerfile` = the suite's canonical skeleton with one of the lines above AFTER the `ln -s` line; `bash g.sh d` → `OK — 1 Dockerfile(s) … 1 of 1 clean`, rc 0 (both modes); the same fixture against `git show a0ad0a084:…` → `::error::… the re-link runs BEFORE the last instruction that writes node_modules`, rc 1. Evidence `20_regression_fixture_full_output.txt`, `08_falsification.out`, `10_extra_shapes.out`, `17_finding4_at_base.out`. Severity Major (a false CLEAN reproduces the #851 outage class); likelihood in operation low — the 25-file corpus writes none of these spellings in any stage, and it takes an author placing an install after the re-link AND spelling it with a prefix.

**Why #879 merged anyway (Wednesday's ruling, stated so it can be read):** against develop M38 the head CLOSES 14 false-clean spellings the corpus does write (`npm run` ×50: bare `yarn`, `npm run build`, `yarn --frozen-lockfile`, `npm init <spec>`, `npm init foo --yes`, `(npm ci)`, `npm install-test`, `npm exec`, bare `npm`, `npm -vv`, `npm --version=1`, `yarn add`, `npm audit fix`, `npm prune` — each rc 0 at M38 / rc 1 at head) and OPENS the 12 above, which the corpus never writes; likelihood-weighted the merge reduces the open false-clean surface, and the class already has this ticket as its home with the class-(a) build queued behind #879's merge.

**Five pre-existing shapes of the same family (the gate's observations; not named here before — searched this ticket for `heredoc` (the false-BLOCK direction only), `RUN [` 0, wrapper words 0):** `if … then npm ci … fi` · `for … do … done` · `{ npm ci; }` · `RUN ["npm","ci"]` (the JSON exec form, which the COPY clause already normalises and the RUN clause does not) · a heredoc body carrying the install after the re-link.

**Fix-shape (the gate's, prose):** stop trusting the leading word alone — after the leading-word pass, ALSO scan every token of the segment: a whole-word manager token (boundary class excluding `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, so `mynpm` still misses and `/usr/local/bin/npm`, `"npm"`, `corepack npm` all hit) whose FOLLOWING token is not on the read-only/probe allowlists is a write — the base's substring instrument re-admitted with a left boundary; it can only ADD writes (fails safe, the file's own stated principle). A wrapper-skip list (`env`+assignments, `exec`, `time`, `nice`, `nohup`, `command`, `xargs`, `sudo` with flags, `then`, `do`, `else`, `{`, `(`) is the deny-list alternative and fails open on the next wrapper. Separately normalise RUN's JSON exec form as the COPY clause does, and read heredoc bodies as RUN text (or deny a final stage that contains a heredoc after the last write — the fail-closed reading).

**Regression cells (the gate's, described):** one cell per spelling above, each expecting exit 1 and the A-clause message; negative controls `RUN echo npm ci` and `RUN mynpm i` expecting 0, so the widened match cannot resurrect the argument-position false block; a cell asserting `RUN ["npm", "ci"]` after the re-link is a write.

**FINDING 2 (Minor, recommendation only):** `npm cache clean --force` / `npm cache verify` as a standalone RUN after the re-link false-BLOCK at the head (rc 0 at base) — the read-only allowlist at `check-shared-relink.sh:203` has no `cache`; corpus 0; in practice joined to the install with `&&`. Consider `cache` for the allowlist, with a cell.

Facts only; no state change on this ticket by the merge seat.

**Record from the #879 review (2026-09-08, finding 4) — four residual false cleans, routed here by the reviewer; not fixed on #879.** Measured by him at `79f1fcb48` and identical on the base `a0ad0a084` (not regressions): `RUN /usr/local/bin/npm ci --omit=dev` — clean (an absolute path defeats the whole-token manager-name match) · `RUN npx create-vite my-app` — clean (`npx` is not in the manager set) · `RUN corepack yarn install` — clean (`corepack` is not stepped over the way `sudo` is) · `RUN sh -c "npm ci"` — clean (the manager sits inside a quoted argument). His read: the natural limit of a line-oriented guard, better on a ticket than as scope creep in that PR. Searched this ticket's description and comments for `corepack`, `npx create-`, `/usr/local/bin/npm` and `sh -c` before writing: 0 hits (control `heredoc` = 1) (s229, 2026-09-14). This ticket's own F-3/F-6/F-7 residue is unchanged by #879 (markers re-read at its head 2026-09-14).

**Held open — a residue by this ticket's own words; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass** (card secuura-fourteen-merged-own-pr-tickets-never-moved, close-by-residue; re-verified at source by s218).
- Residue (comment 240e6985, 2026-09-06): "F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes — NOT fixed, deliberately. Both measured as false blocks … Friction, not danger, so they queue behind the false cleans. Next unless reordered." No later comment closes them. Landed since: F-6 (nginx) via ff7704135 and rounds 1–3 (suite cells `F-6:` at `:506-546`, `F-6 inv:` `:638-642`); F-7's shape in kind (the exemption pin at `:506`).
- Develop probe (read 2026-09-14 at `8861e62161466c40f08d2b10a30edeb203123993`): `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-shared-relink.sh:218-224` (blob `7426b1874bbb`) documents "heredoc bodies land here, which is why RUN <<EOT disqualifies a stage by itself" — the heredoc false block is now a stated rule, not a fix; no suite cell names a runtime stage that is not the last FROM. KS-957 (Backlog, unassigned) carries F4/F5/F6 claim-level residues and 0 hits for heredoc / non-final.
- PRs #876 merged 2026-09-07T00:49:35Z as `8aefd2b06bf29bcac099ce3a1af49bf7f89608fc` and #886 merged 2026-09-07T00:50:26Z as `61df129e9c580e3b4622d9b5de11f2abd765b8f6`; #874 (`6f7885602`) and #879 (`79f1fcb48`) OPEN, both attached. Lane family: L8.
- Stays open; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass. No state write, nothing deployed, no environment touched.

**Round 3 pushed — `a15a5146ec22b515c5f35911dc7c59953375558e`, PR #876.** Kam authorised exactly one narrow round, regression only.

**The regression, and it was larger than the one spelling the verdict named.** Round 2's boundary class `[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]` treats `-`, `.` and `_` as word characters, so a runtime name carrying a version or variant suffix was invisible. Ten shapes were **rc 1 at base `306d0db92` and rc 0 `A_EXEMPT` at round-2 head `3047bcb1d`** — regressions against base, not gaps:

`node-22` · `node22` · `node.22` · `node_22` · `nodejs-22` · `node-lts` · `npx` in the final CMD · `apk add nodejs-current` · the `nodejs.org` tarball install · `apt-get install nodejs-legacy`

The successor brief named six (the suffixed spellings). The gate's own F2 named four more, each also rc 1 at base — so all ten are inside "regression only" and all ten are closed. `npx` is the odd one: not a suffix problem at all, it named the tooling and sat in neither token list, so it joined the tooling clause rather than the word-arm.

**The fix mirrors what the file already did.** `base_is_js_runtime` has always allowed the suffix — `^(node|nodejs|bun|deno)([0-9._-]|$)` — fifteen lines from the clause that did not. The trailing class now matches it instead of inventing a second convention.

**The price, pinned rather than left to be found.** `node-red` is now denied and that is correct (it IS a JS runtime). `node-exporter` is now denied and that is a **false block**, accepted knowingly: this arm fails toward blocking, which a human sees, over exempting, which nobody sees, and no class file reaches the arm today. Both are cells. The false-block class as a whole is gate finding F3 — out of scope by the regression-only ruling.

**Evidence.** All ten measured at three SHAs over the same fixture before the fix was written. Plant-point control run first: the suite's own green shape reads `rc 0 A_OK` at all three guards and the same file minus one re-link line reads `rc 1` at all three. Suite 71 → **86 passed, 0 failed**. Red-proof A (revert the class only) reds **exactly 11** cells, both pair controls and all 71 pre-existing cells green; red-proof B (drop `npx` only) reds **exactly 1**. Both restored by inverse edit, sha256 byte-identical, suite re-run green. Leg 13 on the real tree unchanged: rc 0, 25 Dockerfiles, 4 copy / 21 re-install. Full 13-leg pre-push preflight passed.

Claim-level findings F4/F5/F6 aggregated on **KS-957**, not fixed here.

## F-3: two of the five shapes are FALSE CLEANS on the #851 outage, not friction — fixed in [#876](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/876) @ `af954c691`

**This ticket's framing needs correcting on one point, and it is the one that matters.** F-3 is
written as five *legitimate shapes the parser cannot read*, with live exposure zero. Live exposure
**is** zero — I re-confirmed it — but two of the five are not readability problems. **They are false
cleans on the exact clobber the guard exists to catch.**

Measured on the merged guard at `066cff675`, each fixture being the canonical clobber file with
**only the spelling of the last `node_modules` write changed**, `SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1`:

| the last write | rc | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules` | **1** | blocked — *control* |
| `COPY ["--from=builder", "/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |
| `COPY --from=builder ["/app/node_modules", "./node_modules"]` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |
| `RUN npm i --omit=dev` | **0** | `1 of 1 clean` |

### Why this hid, and why it belongs to the KS-926 family

On a file with **no other parseable write**, these shapes *do* exit 1 — through the
`writes node_modules nowhere (unexpected shape)` **fallback**, whose message is factually wrong about
the file. Reading only the exit code, the guard looks like it handles them.

**The fallback is the only thing between the parser gap and the false clean, and it stops standing
there the moment the file carries a write the parser CAN read** — which all 25 real files do. That is
the campaign's "which clause judged it" question arriving inside this ticket, so the new cells assert
the **clause**, not the exit code: exit-code-only cells would have passed against the unfixed guard.

### Fixed

- `COPY` — normalise JSON/exec array punctuation before the destination test (the test took the last
  whitespace token, `"./node_modules"]`, bracket and quotes attached). **Widening what the parser sees
  can only add writes, never remove one — this direction fails safe.**
- `RUN` — `npm i` writes the same tree as `npm install`. `([ \t]|$)` stops it swallowing `npm init`,
  and a cell pins that.

**Red-proofed separately:** removing the `COPY` normalisation → **28 passed, 2 failed** (exactly the
two JSON cells); reverting `(ci|install|i)` → **29 passed, 1 failed** (exactly the `npm i` cell). Each
tamper restored by inverse edit, byte-identical by sha256. Suite **26 → 30**. Real tree unchanged at
**25 of 25 clean** in both modes.

### Where the rest of this ticket stands

- **F-6 (nginx) — sent to Wednesday as a DECISION, no code**, per her instruction. Made concrete
  first: `a_plain` (nginx final, no node_modules) rc 1; **`b_relink_anyway` — adding the re-link
  honestly — ALSO rc 1**, because the rule anchors on a `node_modules` write and there is none to
  anchor to; `c_pointless_write` (install a node tree into the nginx image purely to satisfy the
  check) rc 0. **The guard's one route to green makes the image worse.** My recommendation is option A
  (exempt a final stage that writes no `node_modules` and copies no builder tree), with the cost named:
  it changes the shape of F-7's cell.
- **F-7 — still blocked on F-6**, exactly as this ticket says. Under option A its cell would pin the
  *exemption* rather than the failure. Whoever takes it should be told that before starting.
- **F-3's heredoc and non-final-stage shapes — NOT fixed, deliberately.** Both measured as false
  *blocks* (rc 1, `final stage has NO re-link`, on a file that re-links inside a `RUN <<EOT` body, and
  on one whose runtime stage is not the last `FROM`). Friction, not danger, so they queue behind the
  false cleans. Next unless reordered.

### Live exposure re-confirmed, with a control

**7** frontend Dockerfiles, **6** with an nginx final stage, **0** consuming `shared-builder`; and
across all **35** Dockerfiles in the tree, **zero** JSON-form `COPY` and **zero** `npm i` — against a
positive control of **25** files that *do* consume `shared-builder`, so the zeros discriminate.

### One thing I did not assert

I reasoned that this ticket's own F-3 example — `COPY ["--from=builder", …]`, flag *inside* the array
— is invalid Docker, and was about to write that down. `docker build --check` reports
**"Check complete, no warnings found"** for both spellings, so I make no such claim; I did not build
either. The fix handles both, and the unambiguously valid spelling has the same hole, so nothing rests
on it.
